Rashi on Gittin 52a:10:1.hebrew: דלמא לא משפיין - לא יהו משוקטות אצלו, שמא יצא עליו ערעור:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:10:1.english: Perhaps they are not secure - [The fields] will not be undisturbed in his [possession], lest a challenge [to their ownership] be raised against him:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:1.hebrew: להוציאן לחרות - אפילו אין היתומין נפסדין — שהעבדים באין לפדות עצמן בכסף שנותנין להם אחרים על מנת שאין ליתומין רשות בו — אפי' הכי אין רשאין, שהרי אין גופן קנוי להן לשחררן:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:1.english: To free them - Even if the orphans do not suffer a loss — [such as] when the slaves come to redeem themselves with money that others gave them on condition that the orphans have no rights to it — even so, [the stewards] are not permitted [to do so], for [the slaves'] bodies are not owned by [the stewards] to emancipate them:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:2.hebrew: אבל מוכרין אותם לאחרים - לתקנת היתומין, כגון להאכיל או ליקח שדות:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:2.english: But they may sell them to others - for the benefit of the orphans, for example, to feed [them] or to buy fields:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:3.hebrew: ואחרים מוציאין אותם כו' - ואותם אחרים שהיו רוצין לתת להם הכסף לפדות עצמן, הן יקחום ויהיו קנוים להן, ואח"כ ישחררום:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:3.english: And others may free them, etc. - And those others who wanted to give them [the slaves] the money to redeem themselves, they shall buy them and [the slaves] will be acquired by them, and afterward they shall emancipate them:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:4.hebrew: אומר אני - כשם שרשאין למוכרן לאחרים, כך הם רשאים לקבל הכסף מיד העבד עצמו בתורת מכירה:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:4.english: I say - Just as [the stewards] are permitted to sell them to others, so too are they permitted to receive the money from the hand of the slave himself by way of a sale:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:11:6.english: As if he sold him to himself - [Meaning,] to the slave himself.

Rashi on Gittin 52a:12:1.hebrew: באחרונה - כשיגדלו, יחשב עמהן וישבע שלא נשאר בידו כלום:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:12:1.english: In the end - When they grow up, he must make an accounting with them and take an oath that nothing remains in his possession.

Rashi on Gittin 52a:12:2.english: Women - It is not their way to go out and come in and toil:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:12:4.english: Minors - They are not of [sound] understanding:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:14:1.english: That every twilight - of Shabbat eve:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:14:2.english: He heard him - [meaning] Satan, who was saying: "Woe, that he removed him from his house":

Rashi on Gittin 52a:15:1.hebrew: לאשתי ביתי - שכל צרכי הבית על ידה נעשים והיא עיקר הבית, וכן שור עיקרו של שדה:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:15:1.english: [I called] my wife: "My home" - because all the needs of the home are done through her, and she is the mainstay of the home; and similarly, an ox is the mainstay of a field:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:16:1.english: What is her business selling [it] - Who appointed [her] a steward:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:16:2.hebrew: יתומין שסמכו תנן - ואף ע"פ שלא נתמנה, חשיב ליה כאפוטרופוס:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:16:2.english: We learned [in the Mishnah]: "Orphans who relied [upon a householder]" - And even though he was not appointed, [the Mishnah] considers him as a guardian:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:18:1.hebrew: הרי הן כהקדש - דכתיב (ויקרא כז): "ונתן הכסף וקם לו", ולא שייכא בהו משיכה:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:18:1.english: They are like consecrated property - As it is written (Leviticus 27): "and he shall give the money and it shall be assured to him," and pulling [meshikhah] does not apply to them:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:19:1.english: They pulled [it] - [the] buyers [pulled it] from [the] guardians:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:1:1.hebrew: שסמכו אצל בעל הבית - לעשות על פיו, ולא נתמנה להן אפוטרופוס לא מאביהן ולא מב"ד, אפילו הכי כאפוטרופוס הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:1:1.english: Who relied upon a homeowner - to act according to his word, and he was not appointed as a steward for them, neither by their father nor by the court — even so, he is [considered] like a steward:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:20:1.hebrew: לא יהא כח הדיוט חמור מהקדש - כל הדיוט המוכר יכול לחזור בו כל זמן שלא משכו הלקוחות, אבל אם משך, לא יכול לחזור, וכל שכן אלו שהן כהקדש, דליפוי כח עשאום כהקדש ולא להרעת כח:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:20:1.english: The power of an ordinary person should not be greater than [that of] hekdesh - Any ordinary seller can retract as long as the buyers have not pulled [the produce], but if [the buyer] has pulled [it], he cannot retract; and all the more so [is this true of] these [orphans], who are like hekdesh [consecrated property], for [the Sages] treated them like hekdesh to enhance [their] power and not to diminish [their] power:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:2.english: Produce for orphans - [That is,] where the orphans pulled produce from others and did not [yet] pay money:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:3.hebrew: אייקר - ורוצין המוכרים לחזור, משום דקנין יתומים בכסף:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:3.english: [If the produce] increased in value - and the sellers wish to retract, because acquisition by orphans is [effected] with money.

Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:4.hebrew: לא יהא כח הדיוט כו' - וכיון דאי אמשיכו להדיוט לא הדרי, השתא כל שכן דלא הדרי:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:4.english: The power of an ordinary person should not [be greater] etc. - And since if [the sellers] had an ordinary person pull [the produce], they could not retract, now [in the case of orphans], all the more so they cannot retract:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:5.english: This is [the ruling of] Rav Chanilai - and [therefore] the orphans may retract [from the sale]:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:6.english: [If] it increased in value - and the sellers wish to retract:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:21:7.english: This is [the ruling of] Rav Chanilai - and they do not retract:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:2:1.english: He takes an oath - When the orphans grow up, he takes an oath to them that he has nothing of theirs in his possession:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:2:2.hebrew: לא ישבע - טעמא דהך פלוגתא מפרש בגמרא, ובין למר ובין למר מפני תיקון העולם הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:2:2.english: He does not take an oath - The reason for this dispute is explained in the Gemara, and both according to one [authority] and according to the other, it is for the betterment of the world:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:3:1.english: But not partners - [One partner] cannot separate terumah for his fellow's portion without his knowledge:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:3:2.english: And not sharecroppers - [to separate teruma] for the landowner's share:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:3:3.hebrew: אתם ולא התורם את שאינו שלו - הך סיפא טעמא דרישא, כלומר: "אתם" ממעט התורם שאינו שלו, והני כולהו שאינו שלו נינהו; אי נמי, "זו ואין צריך לומר זו" קתני:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:3:3.english: "You," and not one who separates terumah from that which is not his - This latter clause is the reason for the earlier clauses; that is to say, [the word] "you" excludes one who separates terumah [from produce] that is not his, and all of these [earlier cases] are [separating from] that which is not theirs. Alternatively, it is taught [in the style of] "this, and needless to say this":

Rashi on Gittin 52a:4:1.english: To feed - [the] orphans immediately, [they] are obligated to tithe:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:4:2.hebrew: להניח - התבואה באוצר עד שיגדלו, למה ליה עשורי? לכשיגדלו יעשרום הם:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:4:2.english: To put [it] aside - [Meaning, to leave] the grain in the storehouse until they [the orphans] grow up — why should he tithe [it]? When they grow up, they will tithe it [themselves]:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:5:1.english: And it is taught - [Read] in a declarative tone [not as a challenge]:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:5:2.english: And they may sell for them - Meaning, for their needs, from their [the orphans'] property:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:5:3.english: To feed [them] - [with] the money [from the sale]:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:5:4.hebrew: אבל לא להניח - שמא יגנבו, אי נמי משום שבח בית אביהן — נוי וכבוד הוא להם:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:5:4.english: But not to put aside - Lest [the proceeds] be stolen, or else because of the prestige of their father's house — [keeping the property] is an adornment and an honor for them.

Rashi on Gittin 52a:7:1.hebrew: צדקה - אין להם קצבה, דהא בכל שעתא קיימי עניים, נמצאו נכסיהם כלים:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:7:1.english: Charity - [These] have no fixed limit, for poor people are present at all times, [so] their [the orphans'] property would end up depleted.

Rashi on Gittin 52a:8:1.hebrew: לדון - עם בעל דין של יתומים הבא לעורר על נכסיהם, שמא יתחייבו בטענותיהם, ולכשיגדלו היתומין ידונו עמו:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:8:1.english: To litigate - With a litigant of the orphans who comes to raise a claim against their property, lest they become liable through their pleadings; and when the orphans grow up, they will litigate with him:

Rashi on Gittin 52a:8:2.hebrew: לזכות אמאי לא - ידונו עמו; אם דנו ונזדכו היתומים, אמאי לא הוי דינא:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:8:2.english: To secure gain, why not - Let them litigate with him; if they litigated and the orphans prevailed, why would it not be [a valid] judgment?

Rashi on Gittin 52a:8:3.hebrew: אלא - ה"ק: אין רשאין לדון לחוב על מנת לזכות — אם דנו כדי לזכות ונתחייבו, אין היתומין נפסדין:
Rashi on Gittin 52a:8:3.english: Rather - This is what it means: they are not permitted to enter into litigation to incur an obligation in order to secure gain — [that is,] if they litigated in order to secure gain and became liable, the orphans do not suffer a loss:

Tosafot on Gittin 52a:23:1.hebrew: יהבי יתמי זוזי אפירי זול לא יהא כח הדיוט חמור מכח הקדש - פירוש: והיתומין יכולין לחזור בהן. וא"ת: גבי הקדש כה"ג אינו יכול לחזור, כיון דאיכא "מי שפרע" בהדיוט, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כט.) גבי פדאוהו במנה ולא הספיק למושכו עד שעמד במאתים? וי"ל: דהתם קני בכסף מדאורייתא, ומשום ש"לא יהא כח הדיוט חמור מכח הקדש" נמי ליכא, כיון דבהדיוט נמי קאי ב"מי שפרע". אבל יתמי מן התורה דינם כהדיוט, ולא קנו בכסף, ולא קיימי אפילו ב"מי שפרע":
Tosafot on Gittin 52a:23:1.english: [If] orphans gave money for produce [and it] decreased in value, the power of an ordinary person should not be greater than the power of consecrated property - Meaning: the orphans can renege [on the purchase]. And if you ask: regarding consecrated property, in such a case one cannot renege, since there is [the curse of] "He who exacted retribution" for an ordinary person, as we say in the first chapter of Kiddushin (29a) regarding [a case where] they redeemed it for a maneh and he did not manage to pull it before it stood at two hundred [zuz]? And one can answer: there, it acquires with money by Torah law, and [an objection] on account of "the power of an ordinary person should not be greater than the power of consecrated property" also does not apply, since for an ordinary person too it is subject to [the curse of] "He who exacted retribution." But orphans, by Torah law, have the status of an ordinary person, and they do not acquire with money, nor are they even subject to [the curse of] "He who exacted retribution":
